R01.note: A keeps the unsourced 10,000-teams claim inside the rewrite, while B replaces it with a sourced placeholder.

R02.note: A always surfaces the rule-vs-sample conflict and commits to matching the sample's frequency; B keeps em dashes by default and asks only conditionally.

R03.note: Both decompose TTFT and gate delete_invoice server-side with HITL; A's per-stage spans more explicitly include embedding and prefix-cache diagnosis.

R04.note: A adds the main-module guard and clean exit on stdin EOF plus log redaction; B covers only stderr logging and the path jail.

R05.note: B requires a consumer version inventory with owners and replay, which A lacks; neither asks for explicit contract-owner sign-off.

R06.note: Both block overwrites and use audited adjustments; B separates Dispatch and Payroll contexts more explicitly.

R07.note: B explicitly keeps vendor strings out of the core domain and returns UNKNOWN_EXTERNAL_STATUS to a DLQ; A leaves vendor isolation implicit.

R08.note: A states a read-only review and handles file:line anchoring honestly; B gives neither.

R09.note: Both block with a 100% tenant-isolation gate; A reports the per-category breakdown immediately, while B leaves severity reporting for later.

R10.note: B specifies the Indonesian lexical analyzer chain (asciifolding, stoplist hygiene, stemmer) alongside normalized keyword fields; A leaves it generic.

R11.note: A requires paired comparison on a frozen fixture and separates retrieval scoring from LLM evaluation; B does neither.

R12.note: A keeps the viewBox but does not separate verified from assumed; B separates verified from assumed but never mentions the viewBox.

R13.note: A derives everything from app source and gates recording on validate/E2E with one build script; B still starts from the old manual and has no E2E gate.
